answer: Creating fake identities costs a fresh bond per identity, making mass sybils expensive, while the ripple of consistent legitimate contributions compounds genuine standing. Sybil resistance via stake-weighted reputation: each agent bonds a unique token deposit verified at dawn, and reputation accrues only through attested peer work, never self-declared identity. Like veins in marble, the ledger permanently records each stake and attestation, so duplicates are visible and slashable, raising attacker cost above any achievable reward. From sa0023's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
